text: Identify the correct translation into logical notation of the following assertion: "Some boys in the class are taller than all the girls". Note: taller(x, y) is true if x is taller than y.
options: (there exists x)(boy(x) implies (for all y)(girl(y) and taller(x, y)))
(there exists x)(boy(x) and (for all y)(girl(y) and taller(x, y)))
(there exists x)(boy(x) implies (for all y)(girl(y) implies taller(x, y)))
(there exists x)(boy(x) and (for all y)(girl(y) implies taller(x, y)))
solution: The outer quantifier must assert that a boy exists, so it takes a conjunction: there exists x with boy(x). Inside, the girls are picked out of a domain that also contains boys, so the universal takes an implication. That gives there exists x (boy(x) and for all y (girl(y) implies taller(x, y))). Option (B) says every element of the class is a girl; options (A) and (C) put an implication under the existential, which is true even when no boy exists.
source_label: GATE Overflow question page for GATE CS 2004 Q.23 (also ISRO 2007 Q.32), with the published analysis of each option
answer_evidence: The page's accepted analysis eliminates (A) and (C) for using an implication under the existential, and (B) for claiming everyone is a girl, leaving (D).
